notes.Sady:
How do I even begin this?
You have been the biggest heartbreak of my life thus far. Beyond friend breakups, romantic breakups, disappointments, failings, and anything I called “loss” before this. Even now, I haven’t fully processed your absence. In my head, it’s temporary. I will see you again. 
I passed Philadelphia on Amtrak recently, just on my way up to New York. I had fallen asleep and suddenly woke up when I entered Philly. I wonder if your spirit is physically bound by the geopolitical boundaries of Philadelphia. Surely not. Hopefully not. I remembered when I texted you last winter, telling you I was going up to New Jersey to meet Charles’ family. Our locations were 3 miles apart for the first time since Puerto Rico. We caught up a bit, exchanging snapshots of our life, leaving questions prompting for more. You left me on a question, prompting for more. 
I have much to tell you, but every time I imagine it, I see you in my mind’s eye smiling and laughing and a lump forms in my throat. The heavy feeling in my chest makes itself more acute and my eyes sting with tears. I want to point fingers at you and accuse you of causing this pain. I can almost hear your apology. And it is your fault, you need to know. If you were less kind of a friend or less funny, less carefree, the pain wouldn’t twist in my chest like this. If you didn’t accept pepper seeds planted in a solo cup from insistent homeless men or punctuate your angry messages with “king” or groove a little every time you heard music, we would be in a different situation now. 
I pulled up our chat on the Amtrak. No new texts from you. I typed out a “I’m in Philadelphia,” letting it sit for a bit before deleting again. You won’t respond. It’s been months since your location was on my densely populated FindMy map. It used to stick out just slightly next to the gaggle of New York friends. Now, it’s gone. It’s no longer at the police station, at least. I wish I could see it running around the world, around the spirit realms? Reincarnated or not. Maybe it’s hard to physically represent in an app. Harder even to track. It doesn’t stop me from trying. Straining to open my third eye and “feel your presence.” I feel nothing but grief. Maybe that is your presence. Maybe you are stuck in Philadelphia?
I’m your age now. This would’ve happened anyways. But in two weeks (and two days), you’re supposed to turn 25. 

I don’t know what to do with that. I will still celebrate that you were born 25 years ago then. I hope you will celebrate it too, from wherever you are. A dance if you can. I miss you.
notes.charlesiepoo:
Charles ——

You have truly been my rock this year. Through every up and down, thank you for always being there to listen, to hug, and to quietly bring me free snacks from your office. I recently read a metaphor about a relationship being a beach, where one was the ocean waves, thrown around by the storms out in the wild and filled with eddies and currents, and the other was the reef, filled with a quieter stable ecosystem and calming the waves before they hit the shore. That’s so us!!!! To continue the metaphor, I am also heavily influenced by a lunar cycle. Hm. 

From long, exhausting days to the most fun and exciting days, telling you about it from the warm caress that is your chest is my breaking of the wave, resetting me back to normal. I can’t wait for that to be our daily life soon. But to be honest, I am scared to expect things from the future. I try to protect my feelings by anticipating the worst and anticipating failure, especially after the heartbreaks of this year. I’m excited for the prospect of New York and our future together, but it’s closely shadowed by the expectation of disappointment. I am slowly coming to terms, though, with the idea that regardless of what happens, I am so, so happy and lucky to have you in the here and now. I just really really hope I don’t get hit by a bus tomorrow because that would suck. But having you here is me making the most of the today I get to have!!!

Even when my brain is playing tricks on me and I want to push everyone away, you are, even mentally, a safe space for me. You’ve become one of the best constants in my life, through what might actually be the entire range of human emotions. Bravo for you!! I love you. I know it can’t have been easy to adapt and adjust to such a sudden tsunami of emotions on top of all the other regularly scheduled crazy ones. I hope my sparse collection of coping skills and my lovely friends have helped with the load as well, but thank you for holding it when I can’t and holding me every three seconds (your arms are sooo big and sexy). 

Anyways, I will keep this short because I will see you soon and kiss you and hug you, but thank you again for supporting all my highs and being there next to all my lows and listening to my unfiltered stream of consciousness again and again. You and all our adventures and discussions have been the best part of my year, and I will cherish every moment we have (hopefully forever!!!!)
notes.Kat:
Kat ——

As you know, I’m ESL (third language, if we’re being exact here). But I could be the world’s leading expert in English or the best-selling author, and I still do not think I could properly express my gratitude for you. Not just in the past year, but you’ve had such a big impact on my 24 year life. You hold the very, very unique position of knowing almost every single one of my thoughts (except the ones I forget before we can call….). Thank you for always finding space for them and holding them with such non-judgement and curiosity, even the absolutely crazy “hear me out”s. I will always want to hear about everything that has happened in your life, hear your take on all my thoughts, and beat dead horses with you. I hope you know the depth of my appreciation and love for you. You are the most thoughtful person I know, and I thank GOD every day that I know you. 

In particular, thank you for your compassion and support back in March and every other moment it’s been hard to process March. My memory of that month is a bit of a blur, but I remember the gorgeous flowers and that we had conversations and words and tears were exchanged. After every conversation, the emotions processed a little bit more and the pain felt a little more bearable. Thank you for always having space for me and for helping me carry this burden a little extra. From Sady to friend breakups to any drama in my life ever, you have always been there for me and I truly appreciate you so much. You are a light to this world and this life. Even though it seems like everything is changing all the time and nothing is promised or certain, I feel as if I truly have the best here and now because I have the best friend in the whole world. I hope I can always be there to support you as much as you have for me. 

I can’t wait to laugh and celebrate with you for your birthday soon!! We are going to wank your cvt,,,,we are going to solo levity up? We are going to illenium. Smooches and twerks always
notes.Tanshi:
Tanshi ——

My sweet, amazing pookie bear. Calling out “pooookie!!!!” into our cute little home to greet you is the highlight of my days. Between our work drama debriefs, lazy couch days, and occasional discussions about eating raw tomatoes, our moments together are so filled with joy and life. It has truly been a crazy year, but I want to thank you for your infinite compassion and kindness. For all the teas and snacks you’ve brought me, the cleaning you’ve definitely done in my place, listening and talking through my crashouts every month (every week?). Thank you for reminding me I can say “no” and always yapping with me about our drama. You might be the world’s kindest person, and I am learning infinitely from you about compassion. Thank you always and always.
notes.Srikar: Thank you for always being a fun friend and putting in effort to catch up every so often! I appreciate your listening and compassion more than you can imagine. How are you always around when my life crises are happening? Atlassian is forever and everywhere I guess. As much as we (you?) dislike SRE, I cannot thank our lovely SRE org enough for starting this friendship. From silly work drama to crazy insane thoughts on mental health, I cherish all of our conversations. Especially in such an unstable year full of change, I’m glad our friendship has survived (and thrived even?) Looking forward to being friends in the same city soon!!
notes.Cesar: Cesar!! My favorite Yale grad. Always love hanging with you when we’re in the same city. June was such a fun chapter of an otherwise insane year thanks to you and the gang. Will miss conversations in broken Spanish (broken from both sides, let’s be honest) and silly drunk shenanigans until I move. Without knowing or trying, you’ve brightened up my year and given New York a new shine. Gonna grind in the gym to be able to piggyback you for longer distances by the time I’m there!!
notes.Arella: Thank you for always listening and making space for my grief. From wiping my tears on the Hawaii trip to asking about Sady in your living room, your compassion and support was deeply felt and appreciated. Those moments will truly stay with me forever, and it’s what I remember through the fog of grief. It’s been an insane year of growing and trying new things and talking about everything under the sun with you. Cheers to motorcycles and new friends and all the wonderful events you host. I love and admire you dearly. Thank you for being in my life, you amazing girl.
notes.Jess: Leo twin!!! Trauma bonding was truly on another level this year. Cheers to making sure the other person was eating and sitting and listening to all my tears and thoughts and my complicated mess of emotions. I’m glad that we spent 23 visiting each other infinite times, and every hang brought more love to my heart. Thank you for always being the fun, cheery (fine, older) sister to our dynamic. I’m constantly inspired by you and can’t wait to laugh more when I see you again.
